briefTitle: A Study of Novel EGFR TKI and ADC Combination in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
officialTitle: A Phase 1/2 Multi-Center Open-Label Study Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of Novel EGFR-Targeted Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor in Combination With TROP2 Antibody-Drug Conjugate in Patients With EGFR-Mutant Advanced or Metastatic NSCLC After Progression on Osimertinib
leadSponsor: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center / Daichi Sankyo
summary: This study tests whether combining a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate with targeted therapy can overcome secondary resistance mutations in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced lung adenocarcinoma who have previously progressed on first-line third-generation EGFR inhibitors.

inclusionCriteria: Histologically or cytologically confirmed locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (Stage IV).
Documented sensitizing EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion or L858R point mutation) by CAP/CLIA-certified genomic assay.
Radiographically documented disease progression during or after treatment with at least one prior line of EGFR-TKI (including osimertinib, lazertinib, or equivalent).
Age >= 18 years at the time of signing informed consent.
ECOG Performance Status of 0 or 1 with an estimated life expectancy of >= 12 weeks.
At least one measurable lesion according to RECIST v1.1 criteria.

Adequate organ and bone marrow function: Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) >= 1.5 x 10^9/L, Platelets >= 100 x 10^9/L, Hemoglobin >= 9.0 g/dL, Serum Creatinine <= 1.5x upper limit of normal (ULN), Total Bilirubin <= 1.5x ULN.
exclusionCriteria: Presence of symptomatic or untreated active central nervous system (CNS) metastases or leptomeningeal disease. Patients with treated, asymptomatic brain metastases stable for >= 4 weeks are eligible.
Prior treatment with a TROP2- or HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC).
History of clinically significant interstitial lung disease (ILD) or radiation pneumonitis requiring systemic corticosteroid therapy.
Significant cardiovascular impairment: LVEF < 50%, QTcF prolongation > 470 ms, or New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class >= II congestive heart failure.
Active uncontrolled systemic infection (HIV, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C requiring antiviral therapy).

briefTitle: Evaluation of KRAS G12C Inhibitor Combined With Cetuximab in Refractory Colorectal Cancer
officialTitle: A Phase 2 Multicenter Study of Second-Generation KRAS G12C Covalent Inhibitor (Divarasib) in Combination With Anti-EGFR Monoclonal Antibody (Cetuximab) in Patients With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
summary: This clinical trial investigates the clinical benefit and tumor response rate of a potent KRAS G12C selective covalent inhibitor paired with EGFR receptor blockade to shut down vertical pathway reactivation in pre-treated metastatic colorectal cancer.

inclusionCriteria: Histologically confirmed advanced, unresectable or metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma.
Identification of KRAS G12C mutation in tumor tissue or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) by validated molecular profiling.
Prior progression on or intolerance to fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy regimens (e.g., FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, or FOLFOXIRI).
Age >= 18 years.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Adequate renal, hepatic, and hematologic reserve (Serum creatinine <= 1.5x ULN, AST/ALT <= 3.0x ULN without liver metastases or <= 5.0x ULN with liver metastases).
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.
exclusionCriteria: Prior treatment with a KRAS G12C targeted inhibitor (adagrasib, sotorasib, or investigative covalent G12C agents).
Presence of concurrent BRAF V600E mutation or high microsatellite instability (MSI-H / dMMR) eligible for checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy.
Active brain metastases or history of carcinomatous meningitis.
Corrected QT interval (QTcF) > 480 ms or history of ventricular arrhythmias.

locations.facility: City of Hope Comprehensive Cancer Center

briefTitle: Novel Bispecific Antibody for PARP-Inhibitor Refractory BRCA1/2 Deficient Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
officialTitle: A Phase 1/2 Open-Label, Multicenter Dose-Escalation and Expansion Trial of Investigational ATR Kinase Inhibitor in Combination With Immunotherapy in Patients With Deleterious Germline or Somatic BRCA-Mutated Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Refractory to Platinum and PARP Inhibitors
summary: A clinical study assessing whether synthetic lethality can be restored by targeting the DNA damage response (DDR) via ATR inhibition in patients with BRCA-mutated triple-negative breast cancer who have experienced disease recurrence after platinum therapy or PARP inhibitors.

inclusionCriteria: Documented metastatic or locally recurrent inoperable triple-negative breast cancer (ER < 1%, PR < 1%, HER2 negative per ASCO/CAP criteria).
Deleterious germline or somatic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation confirmed by sequencing.
Prior treatment with an anthracycline or taxane, and prior treatment with platinum chemotherapy and/or a PARP inhibitor (e.g., olaparib, talazoparib) with documented disease recurrence.
Age >= 18 years of age.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Resolution of all acute toxic effects of prior chemotherapy to NCI CTCAE Grade <= 1.
exclusionCriteria: Evidence of symptomatic CNS metastases or spinal cord compression.
Concurrent treatment with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers.
History of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
Active autoimmune disease requiring high-dose systemic corticosteroids (> 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent).

locations.facility: UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center

briefTitle: Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte (TIL) Cell Therapy Combined With BRAF Inhibition in Refractory Melanoma
officialTitle: A Phase 2 Study of Autologous Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes (Lifileucel) Following Targeted Therapy and Anti-PD-1 Failure in Advanced BRAF-Mutant Cutaneous Melanoma
summary: This trial investigates the antitumor activity of adoptive cell transfer using autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in patients with unresectable Stage IIIc/IV melanoma harboring the BRAF V600 mutation who have progressed through both immune checkpoint inhibitors and BRAF/MEK targeted inhibitors.

inclusionCriteria: Unresectable Stage IIIc or Stage IV cutaneous melanoma.
Presence of BRAF V600E or V600K mutation confirmed by molecular testing.

Prior disease progression on or intolerance to an anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody (e.g., nivolumab, pembrolizumab) AND prior progression on BRAF inhibitor +/- MEK inhibitor therapy (e.g., dabrafenib + trametinib).
At least one resectable lesion (>= 1.5 cm diameter) for generation of TIL product, plus at least one remaining measurable target lesion per RECIST v1.1.
Age 18 to 70 years.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Adequate pulmonary and cardiac status: FEV1 and DLCO >= 60% of predicted, LVEF >= 50% on echocardiogram.
exclusionCriteria: Active, untreated brain metastases (patients with successfully resected or stereotactic radiosurgery treated brain lesions stable for >= 8 weeks are permitted).
Severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or significant cardiac arrhythmia.
Systemic immunosuppressive therapy within 2 weeks of cell infusion.
Prior cell therapy (CAR-T or TCR-engineered T cells).

briefTitle: Next-Generation HER2-Targeted Bispecific Antibody in HER2-Low and Refractory Solid Tumors
officialTitle: A Phase 1/1b Study of Zanidatamab Zovodotin (ZW49) in Patients With Advanced HER2-Expressing or HER2-Amplified Cancers After Progression on Trastuzumab Deruxtecan
summary: Evaluating the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of a biparatopic antibody-drug conjugate directed against two distinct extracellular domains of the HER2 receptor in pre-treated solid tumors.

inclusionCriteria: Locally advanced or metastatic HER2-expressing or HER2-amplified solid tumors (IHC 3+, IHC 2+/ISH+, or HER2-low IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-).
Prior progression on standard systemic therapies, including prior HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugates (e.g., T-DXd).
Age >= 18 years.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1.
exclusionCriteria: Uncontrolled CNS metastases.
Prior severe infusion-related reactions to trastuzumab or related monoclonal antibodies.
LVEF < 50% assessed by ECHO or MUGA scan.

briefTitle: Phase 3 Trial of Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist in Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes with High Cardiovascular and Renal Risk
officialTitle: A Phase 3, Multi-Center, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study Evaluating the Safety and Glycemic Efficacy of Retatrutide (Triple GIP/GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonist) in Adults With Inadequately Controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Established Complications
summary: This study evaluates whether a breakthrough triple agonist (GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptor agonist) achieves superior glycemic control (HbA1c reduction) and renal preservation in patients with poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus despite multi-drug standard therapy.

inclusionCriteria: Documented diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with baseline HbA1c between 7.5% and 10.5% inclusive.
Inadequate glycemic control despite stable treatment for >= 90 days with metformin and/or SGLT2 inhibitor, with or without basal insulin.
Documented diabetic complications: Albuminuria (UACR >= 30 mg/g) or estimated GFR (eGFR) between 25 and 75 mL/min/1.73 m².
Age >= 18 years and <= 75 years at time of screening.
Body Mass Index (BMI) >= 25.0 kg/m².
Stable blood pressure (systolic < 160 mmHg, diastolic < 100 mmHg) on standard antihypertensive regimen.
exclusionCriteria: Diagnosis of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus or history of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).
End-stage renal disease (ESRD) on maintenance dialysis or eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m².
Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
Acute coronary syndrome, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 6 months prior to screening.
History of severe acute or chronic pancreatitis.

locations.facility: Joslin Diabetes Center / Harvard Medical School

briefTitle: Novel Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitor in High-Risk Diabetic Kidney Disease and Resistant Albuminuria
officialTitle: A Phase 3 Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Lorundrostat (Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitor) on Kidney Outcomes and Albuminuria in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Diabetic Nephropathy
summary: This clinical trial assesses the efficacy of targeted aldosterone synthase inhibition in halting the progression of diabetic kidney disease and reducing persistent proteinuria in patients with Type 2 Diabetes who remain at high risk despite ACEi/ARB and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.

inclusionCriteria: Adults aged 18 to 80 years with established Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Persistent macroalbuminuria defined as urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) >= 300 mg/g (or microalbuminuria >= 100 mg/g).
Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) between 25 and 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD Stage 3a or 3b).
Treated with maximum tolerated dose of an ACE inhibitor or ARB and an SGLT2 inhibitor for at least 8 weeks.
Serum potassium <= 4.8 mmol/L at time of screening.
exclusionCriteria: History of adrenal insufficiency or primary hyperaldosteronism.
eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m² or requirement for dialysis within 3 months.
Serum potassium > 5.0 mmol/L at screening.
Uncontrolled hypertension with resting systolic blood pressure >= 180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure >= 110 mmHg.

locations.facility: Johns Hopkins Hospital Comprehensive Diabetes Center
University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
